Description

PEA15 is a small cytoplasmic protein that binds ERK1 and ERK2 and keeps them out of the nucleus, so it blocks ERK-dependent transcription and proliferation, and a nuclear export signal of PEA15 is needed for this anchoring [1]. Bound to PEA15, ERK2 can no longer bind the nucleoporins it needs to cross the nuclear pore [2]. By holding ERK in the cytoplasm PEA15 also limits the invasion of tumour cells [3]. Two serines of PEA15 regulate its hold: protein kinase C phosphorylates Ser104, and calcium-calmodulin dependent kinase II or AKT phosphorylates Ser116 [4, 5]. Only PEA15 phosphorylated on both serines releases ERK, which can then reach its nuclear targets [6].
